learning: Iterations 0 and 1 showed off-track failures at 11-16% progress with max_error about 0.06-0.07 m, and drivetrain changes gave only marginal, track-dependent gains. Forward lead is the next lever to test alone; if it does not help, the constraint is probably gain or speed rather than sensing.
notes: Isolated sensor-lead test: the Builder's geometry with sensor y moved from 0.05 to 0.07 m, and the controller unchanged from iteration 1 so the lead is the only variable. Measures progress, max_error and slalom oscillation against iterations 0 and 1.
rationale: Iterations 0 and 1 both ended all 60 development runs off track at 11-16% progress, with max_error of 0.061-0.070 m against the 0.06 m limit and one line-loss event per run. Steering oscillation stayed low on the oval (0.073), so the robot drifts steadily off the line rather than oscillating. Changing the drivetrain from track 0.12 to 0.10 m and mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg moved the score by only 0.14, so drivetrain is not the binding constraint. This iteration tests the Builder's one remaining sensing lever: forward sensor lead from y = 0.05 to y = 0.07 m, which is inside the 0.08 m limit. I keep the controller identical to iteration 1 (kp 1.25, kd 0.25, ki 0, base_speed 1.5, weights [1.2, 0.6, 0, -0.6, -1.2], last_direction) so any change in progress or max_error can be attributed to the lead. The added lead lets the sensors see the line earlier, so the existing gain should correct earlier on curves. The main risk is overshoot on the slalom, where kd 0.25 is the existing damping. I expect max_error to fall and progress to rise on the oval and s-bend, with steering_oscillation on the slalom staying near the iteration 1 level of about 0.15.
